رَاقِعٌ [act. part. n. of رَقَعَ: see an ex. voce خَرْقٌ]. ―
-b2- It is said in a trad., المُؤْمِنُ وَاهٍ رَاقِعٌ فِالسَّعِيدٌ مَنْ هَلَكَ عَلَى رَقْعِهِ (tropical:) The believer is one who becomes unsound in his religion by his disobe-
dience, and who repairs it by his repentance: [therefore the happy is he who dies while he is repairing:] (TA in the present art.:) i. e., one who offends [and] who repents. (TA in art. وهى.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
